methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective single-center cohort design is reasonable for an initial recurrence-risk analysis, and the authors transparently report a sample-size shortfall (148 vs. planned 233, yielding ~70% power) and apply Peduzzi's 10 events/variable rule to constrain the multivariable Cox model. Statistical handling is competent: Kaplan–Meier estimation, Cox models with Schoenfeld residual checking for proportional hazards, MICE (5 imputations) with Rubin's rules for the two variables with >5% missingness, and bootstrap-based calibration (B=200). Important weaknesses include: no external validation (only apparent/internal bootstrap performance reported), the C-index reported inconsistently (0.630 in abstract, 0.640 and 0.638 in Results/Discussion), no optimism-corrected C-index, treatment-selection bias not formally mitigated (no propensity or IPTW analysis), and the recurrence definition (new lesion within 2 cm of healed field) is itself acknowledged to conflate new field lesions with true relapse. Subgroup/interaction analyses are explicitly labeled exploratory, which is appropriate given low power.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study (Oxford 2b) with a derived prediction model, lacking external validation. Clinical relevance is modest: lesion count and incomplete clearance as predictors of AK recurrence are already well-recognized in the literature, the endpoint is local recurrence (a disease-oriented surrogate, not SCC progression or patient-reported outcomes), and model discrimination is only moderate (C-index ~0.63). The nomogram could inform follow-up intensity but is unlikely to change practice without external validation and inclusion of modern field-directed therapies (as the authors themselves note). Translational path to altered management is plausible but not demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the applicable standard because the primary deliverable is a multivariable Cox prediction model and nomogram, though STROBE elements also apply. Reporting is adequate on study design, inclusion/exclusion, predictor definitions, outcome definition, handling of missing data (MICE with 5 imputations and Rubin's pooling), and apparent performance measures (C-index, Brier, calibration curve). Key TRIPOD gaps include: no clear specification of model type as development vs. validation (effectively development with internal bootstrap only), no reporting of the final nomogram's point allocations or regression equation, no optimism-corrected performance estimates, no decision-curve analysis, no comparison to alternative models, and no participant-flow diagram. There is no data-availability or code-availability statement in the retained text; no repository, code link, or protocol pre-registration is mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is incremental under the empirical-novelty dimension. Lesion burden/field extent and incomplete treatment response are already established predictors of AK recurrence (and cited as such from the authors' own references 9–11, 22, 23), and multiple AK risk-prediction and nomogram efforts exist. The contribution is a single-center retrospective Cox model with internal bootstrap validation—no new biomarker, no novel methodology, and no under-studied population explicitly leveraged. The authors appropriately acknowledge the absence of molecular markers and advanced imaging and that contemporary therapies (e.g., tirbanibulin) are not represented, which further limits novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable, logically organized (Introduction → Methods → Results → Discussion), and the abstract reasonably summarizes the study, though it leaves a small inconsistency with the main text (C-index 0.630 vs. 0.640/0.638). Methods are generally clear, but the inclusion-criteria enumeration is formatted awkwardly (parenthetical numbers mid-sentence), and the sample-size formula has typographic issues (e.g., 'E=(Z1−α/2+Z1−β)2[ln(HR)]2×p×(1−p)' lacks proper subscripts/exponents). The Discussion is thoughtful about field cancerization, clonal kinetics, and real-world treatment evolution (tirbanibulin, urea pre-conditioning), though it occasionally reads as narrative review rather than tightly tied to the results. Figure/table captions are informative but minimal; no participant-flow diagram is included.

key_strengths: Transparent, pre-specified sample-size calculation acknowledging ~70% power and framing subgroup/interaction findings as exploratory
Appropriate handling of missing data with MICE (5 imputations) and Rubin's rules
Proportional-hazards assumption formally tested with Schoenfeld residuals; bootstrap-based calibration (B=200)
Thoughtful discussion of field cancerization, clonal kinetics, and limitations of the 2 cm recurrence definition
Explicit acknowledgment of generalizability constraints given evolving therapies (tirbanibulin, pretreatment strategies)
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with no external validation; only apparent + internal bootstrap performance reported, and no optimism-corrected C-index
Discrimination is modest (C-index ~0.63) and reported inconsistently across abstract (0.630), Results (0.640), and Discussion (0.638)
Findings (lesion burden, incomplete response) are confirmatory of established literature; incremental empirical novelty
TRIPOD reporting gaps: no participant-flow diagram, no regression equation or nomogram point table in text, no decision-curve analysis, no protocol pre-registration
No data-availability or code-availability statement in retained text; reproducibility posture is weak
Treatment-selection bias (confounding by indication) handled only by covariate adjustment; no propensity-score or IPTW sensitivity analysis
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent but highly incremental single-center retrospective prediction-model study with modest discrimination, no external validation, confirmatory findings, and weak reproducibility reporting. Best fit is a Tier 4 oncology/dermatology-adjacent venue, and even there major revisions are needed to address TRIPOD gaps, performance consistency, and validation posture.
